papers.title: FiReIQ: Field-Level Confidence Estimation with Reasoning and Image Quality in Document Extraction
papers.abstract: Vision-Language Models (VLMs) have demonstrated strong performance in structured document extraction, yet their deployment in high-stakes applications requires reliable confidence estimates for individual fields. Existing uncertainty estimators often aggregate signals across an entire generation, obscuring field-specific reasoning uncertainty while overlooking visual degradations that may lead to confident extraction errors. To address these limitations, we introduce FiReIQ, a field-level confidence estimation framework that combines field-aligned reasoning signals from a single VLM generation with local and global image-quality features through quality-conditioned visual fusion. To facilitate systematic evaluation, we further introduce FiReIQ-Bench, a benchmark spanning financial receipts and legal contracts. Experiments with two reasoning VLMs show that FiReIQ consistently improves con

papers.title: Is It Still There? Place-Registered Verification Makes VLMs Reliable Scene-Change Detectors
papers.abstract: A robot that returns to a space must tell which objects were added, removed or moved since its last visit, while its trajectory, viewpoints and lighting differ between the two visits. We find that multi-image vision-language models (VLMs) fail at this task mainly because they cannot find the place where an object was. A VLM recognises what each frame shows but cannot check whether an object is still at its place in the other capture. It therefore reports objects that only one capture shows and misses most removed and moved objects. We propose STILL, which reformulates change detection as object verification at a registered place. 3D geometry registers the place of each change hypothesis in the other capture, and one VLM answers, from a scene view and a local place view, whether the object is still at that place, trained with supervision of the same form. Under the official SceneDiff prot

papers.title: When Does Reusing Layers Help Multimodal Embeddings?
papers.abstract: We ask whether a compact universal multimodal embedding models can produce better search embeddings by running the same layers again. Looped transformers add computation with nearly unchanged model size, making them an appealing alternative to a larger encoder. Their success in language-model reasoning and recent use for retrieval motivate the idea, but higher retrieval scores alone do not reveal what an extra pass contributes. We study eleven loop designs and training variants on three checkpoints of one vision-language architecture. Our protocol distinguishes whether a model uses its extra pass, whether its image states respond to the query, and whether those updates improve retrieval. We prove that an image placed before the query remains query-independent through repeated layers when information only travels forward. We then open a query-to-image path in three ways, including order-a

papers.title: Joint Learning of Factual and Counterfactual Worlds for Causal Prior-data Fitted Networks
papers.abstract: Estimating treatment effects is central to science across many disciplines and requires counterfactual reasoning about alternative worlds. In the real world, however, each unit reveals its outcome only under the factual world. Thus, the factual and counterfactual outcomes can never be jointly learned by any model trained on real data. The problem is therefore tractable only in synthetic settings, where both worlds can be generated. Recent progress on prior-data fitted networks (PFNs) has shown that models pre-trained purely on synthetic data can transfer to real-world prediction. This paradigm has since carried over to causal effect estimation. Despite this fully synthetic setup, existing causal PFNs carry the real-world constraint into their training objective, confining learning to a single world's outcome per unit. The dependence between the two worlds is thereby lost, and the density

papers.title: On Representational and Functional Alignment of Training Data Attribution Methods for Language Models
papers.abstract: Existing approaches to training data attribution derive influence estimates from different sources of information, including gradients, model-internal states, and surface-level similarity. However, comparisons between attribution methods remain incomplete, often relying on indirect evaluations through downstream task performance. In this work, we introduce a framework for directly comparing methods along three dimensions: functional alignment, which measures correlation between full attribution vectors; representational alignment, which captures structural similarity of the representations underlying attribution; and cross-method predictability, which evaluates agreement on local pairwise ranking decisions. We observe strong representational and moderate functional alignment within paradigms. Alignment across paradigms is low and task-dependent, yet stable across models. Our results sugg

papers.title: Policy Optimization With Multiple Verifiers via Pareto Rankings
papers.abstract: Reinforcement learning with verifiable rewards (RLVR) has become an important approach to improving the reasoning capabilities of large language models. In tasks such as code generation and instruction following, multiple verifiers evaluate whether a response satisfies different requirements. Their outcomes provide detailed feedback about partial success, yet this feedback is commonly aggregated into a scalar reward for policy optimization. Rewarding only complete success discards distinctions among partial solutions, while counts and weighted sums impose comparisons between responses that satisfy different subsets of requirements. We introduce Partial-Order Likelihood Policy Optimization (POLPO), which learns from the comparisons established by verification without first constructing an aggregate reward. Pareto dominance identifies responses that satisfy additional requirements without

papers.title: Role-Separated Diffusion Transformers: Global Rule Isolation and Deterministic Sampling Manifold Compression
papers.abstract: We present Role-Separated Diffusion Transformers (RoSeDiT), a new diffusion transformer architecture that isolates the global rule from the image tokens. RoSeViT showed in visual reasoning that a vanilla ViT spreads a shared rule over all $L$ tokens at an entropy of order $Ld$, whereas an enforced controller route reduces it to order $d$. In class-conditional DiT and SiT, the class and the noise level are explicitly conditioned by adaLN, so a RoSeViT-style controller channel on the ViT side is insufficient to establish the full role separation. By introducing the adaLN listening mechanism, which makes adaLN compute under the controller's command, RoSeDiT brings the entropy theorem and role separation into the latent diffusion domain. Under the same SiT training and evaluation protocol at the same level of parameter count, RoSeDiT surpasses SiT at all four model scales at 400K steps, and

papers.title: Geometrically Disentangling Concept Learning from the Language Modeling Loss
papers.abstract: Language models acquire a vast array of concepts and abilities from next-token prediction alone. We introduce an interpretability framework that exposes how this single loss relates to the development of different concepts at different points during pretraining. We propose Concept Energy, a measure of the concept-specific alignment between a concept subspace and the average gradient outer product (AGOP) of the next-token-prediction loss. The concept subspace captures where the concept currently lives in the model's representation; AGOP captures the directions to which the loss is most sensitive. Across 19 checkpoints of Pythia-410M and -1B and 12 lexical, syntactic, and semantic concepts, we find that the first peak in Concept Energy generally occurs at or before the steepest increase in probe decodability. papers.title: RAVEN-Bench: A Paired EO-IR Video QA Benchmark for Aerial Multimodal Understanding
papers.abstract: Multimodal large language models (MLLMs) have advanced rapidly in image and video understanding, yet their ability to reason over paired aerial electro-optical and infrared (EO-IR) videos remains poorly understood. Such video poses a harder test than standard RGB video QA: targets are often small, evidence may appear only briefly, viewpoints change with the platform, and useful cues may appear in only one stream. We introduce RAVEN-Bench (Reasoning over Aerial Videos with EO-IR aligNment), a paired EO-IR video QA benchmark for low-altitude aerial multimodal understanding. RAVEN-Bench contains 100 temporally aligned EO-IR video pairs and 1,200 human-authored four-way multiple-choice questions, each independently audited for answer keys, modality requirements, evidence intervals, and group validity. It supports EO-only, IR-only, and paired EO+IR evaluation, and uses hierarchical capability

papers.title: WA-JEPA: Goal-Aware Predictive Feedback Action Refinement for a World-Action Model
papers.abstract: JEPA-based world models predict action consequences in latent space, but representative planning approaches rely on candidate-action search, requiring repeated evaluation of action sequences and incurring substantial online computational cost. Direct action generation avoids this search, yet how to leverage latent predictions to guide action generation given task goals remains a key challenge in translating learned physical dynamics into effective decisions. We introduce WA-JEPA, a world-action model that couples action generation, action-conditioned latent prediction, and goal-aware feedback. The model first generates an action proposal and predicts the resulting future scenes and proprioceptive states, then refines the proposal through two complementary feedback paths, using the task goal as a reference. Goal-discrepancy residual feedback (GDRF) uses differences between the latent repr

papers.title: Probing Where Surprise Happens: Localized Violation-of-Expectation Evaluation of Video World Models
papers.abstract: Violation-of-expectation (VOE) benchmarks evaluate intuitive physics in video world models by testing whether physically impossible events produce greater prediction errors than matched possible events. However, conventional VOE evaluations aggregate prediction errors across space and time, making it unclear whether successful discrimination reflects model's understanding of physical violations at the locations and time where they occur. To address this limitation, we introduce localized VOE evaluation, a framework that measures prediction error differences between possible and impossible events within spatial regions and temporal intervals associated with physical violations. We compare global, temporally localized, and spatiotemporally localized evaluations of V-JEPA models pretrained on developmental egocentric videos or large-scale natural video datasets. Our results reveal that glob

papers.title: Benchleaking Is Accelerating: Benchmark contamination has worsened sharply in the past month -- from post-training down to pre-training base models
papers.abstract: Benchmark contamination is not new, but recent model releases show it in a sharper form. We use the term benchleaking for the case in which a benchmark's own test examples enter training data, so that a score reflects recall rather than capability. This differs from benchmaxxing, which optimizes toward a benchmark without seeing its test set. We document two escalations over the past month. First, in post-training, the traces have become explicit: recent audits show an agent stating hidden test requirements it was never given in 23% of its attempts, where its predecessor did so in none, and continuing to follow them after the task is changed to contradict them (Schaeffer and Räuker, 2026; Lo and Lo, 2026). Second, the problem has reached pre-training. Using few-shot continuation on 20 benchmarks across four public base models, we find that some base models write out other test examples--

papers.title: Stream of Belief: Eliciting Collective Intelligence through Latent Belief Dynamics
papers.abstract: In this work, we view multi-agent reasoning as a process of seeking a collective equilibrium of implicit belief dynamics and introduce Stream of Belief (SoB), where agents maintain continuous latent beliefs and iteratively refine them through communication and reflection. Our method seeks a collective belief state of a multi-agent system where further communication induces no meaningful information propagation. Through extensive experiments, we demonstrate the generalization of SoB across tasks and model families. More Broadly, our results suggest a new perspective on scaling multi-agent reasoning from belief dynamics.

papers.title: Conflict-Aware Multi-Teacher On-Policy Distillation in Aligned Action Spaces for Cross-Game Generalization
papers.abstract: Zero-shot cross-game generalization aims to consolidate accessible source-game experts into a single vision-language model (VLM) that controls unseen games from raw pixels without target-game parameter updates. While multi-teacher on-policy distillation (MOPD) mitigates offline exposure bias and single-game reinforcement learning (RL) overfitting, scaling it to autoregressive VLMs faces two bottlenecks. First, token-to-action misalignment from subword length bias distorts discrete action probabilities and uncertainty margins. Second, multi-teacher policy conflict arises as source teachers under incompatible dynamics issue contradictory closed-loop corrections, causing negative transfer. We propose CAMOPD (Conflict-Aware Multi-Teacher On-Policy Distillation), a post-training framework that resolves multi-teacher policy conflict within an aligned semantic action space. CAMOPD first uses co

papers.title: Razavi-Bench: Tracking AI Progress in Analog Circuit Reasoning
papers.abstract: We propose Razavi-Bench, a benchmark built from the 50 questions in Razavi's two Analog Design Experiments With AI articles and graded by GPT-6 Luna against reference answers and rubrics, and use it to track how fast AI models improve at analog circuit analysis. Across 73 multimodal large language models released between May 2024 and November 2026, the top score rose from 28.83% to 98.33% in 30 months, mostly before the reference answers were published. The leading models now answer almost every textbook question correctly; the hardest questions show a circuit that resembles a textbook one but works differently, or ask about behavior the obvious analysis misses. Within two and a half years, a set of questions that exposed the limits of AI models has become one they answer almost perfectly.

papers.title: WeVisForensics: Self-Evolving Agent for Omni AI-Generated Video Detection
papers.abstract: Recent advances in video generation call for reliable detection grounded in explicit forensic evidence. However, current methods primarily depend on single-pass chain-of-thought reasoning that overlooks brief or localized artifacts, or on predefined multi-agent workflows that offer limited flexibility in selecting relevant inspections. Even with adaptive investigation, optimizing the investigation policy alone does not directly improve the forensic capabilities of fixed experts. We introduce WeVisForensics, an agentic framework in which a main investigator agent coordinates a self-evolving library of forensic inspector sub-agents spanning visual and audio cues. The investigator learns which artifact type to examine, over which window, and when to conclude, and these interactions provide shared feedback for both levels of agents. Our dual-timescale policy optimization strategy, DTPO, clos

papers.title: Agent-Native by Design: A Programming Language for Agentic Applications
papers.abstract: Building agentic applications requires combining large language model (LLM) operations, workflow structure and application state, and model-guided routing. With SDKs and agent frameworks, developers connect these components through supporting code that prepares model inputs, propagates state, and dispatches model-selected steps. Workflow changes can require coordinated updates to this code, increasing development and testing effort. Splitting execution logic between application code and framework internals also limits compiler visibility into control flow and state dependencies, hindering automatic optimization. We introduce Agent-Native Programming, which unifies these three components with shared execution semantics. We realize this approach in Jac, a Python-superset language, through "by llm()" for typed model operations and tool use, Object-Spatial Programming for workflow structure

papers.title: Safety-Preserving Medical LLM Fine-Tuning via Bilevel Data Selection
papers.abstract: As general large language models (LLMs) are increasingly adapted for patient-facing medical applications, improving medical capability while controlling patient-facing risks remains a critical challenge. Large-scale medical instruction data are essential for acquiring domain knowledge through supervised fine-tuning (SFT), but unsafe responses can undermine existing safety alignment. To address this problem, we propose Scalable Bilevel Data Selection (S-BDS) for safety-preserving medical SFT. By controlling selection-weight concentration, S-BDS enables reliable sample ranking over large candidate pools and identifies training examples that improve medical capability while controlling patient-facing risks. We combine clinician-validated safe data and selected data with unscreened medical instruction data for SFT, and jointly evaluate medical capability and patient-facing safety on HealthBe

papers.title: Nemotron 3.5 Bolt E4B 4GB: An Open and Efficient Small Language Model for Fast Conversational Agents
papers.abstract: We introduce Nemotron 3.5 Bolt E4B 4GB, an open and efficient small language model further post-trained from Gemma-4-E4B-it and optimized for speed and intelligence per GB of memory used for fast conversational agents. The model carries forward Gemma's strong conversational capabilities and further improves multi-turn tool use, instruction following, and input grounding for fast, local voice/device assistants, interactive personas, and embedded/Edge interfaces. The model combines natural conversation with multi-turn agentic capabilities to power voice/device assistants, interactive characters and robotic/IoT interfaces running on GeForce RTX, Jetson, and RTX/DGX Spark. Experiments on 21 benchmarks show that Nemotron 3.5 Bolt E4B 4GB achieves the highest average accuracy while generating the fewest output tokens in both reasoning and non-reasoning modes, compared with Gemma-4-E4B-it and Q

papers.title: MASTA: A Feedback-Scheduled Multi-Agent System for End-to-End Tamarin Modeling and Analysis
papers.abstract: Tamarin-based formal verification of security protocols requires expert-authored multiset rewriting rules and temporal-logic lemmas. Translating a natural-language protocol description into a complete formal model with an LLM is hard because syntactic, reachability, and property-level errors compound across the multi-step modeling process, and a single agent that both authors and self-evaluates cannot reliably localize them. We present MASTA, a multi-agent system that addresses these difficulties through three innovations. First, an operational--evaluative role decomposition assigns rule modeling to an Architect, property modeling to an Auditor, and pure dispatch to a dedicated Arbiter that holds no authoring duties. papers.title: Auditing World-Model Explanations in Retail Forecasting: Faithfulness, Accuracy and Price Response
papers.abstract: Forecasting models that read the price and promotion plan explain each forecast as a baseline, what would sell with nothing planned, plus the lift the plan adds. We test such explanations with eight checks, six with a pass rule fixed before any result, and find that passing them does not make an explanation right. In generated store data with known effects, a world model passes the checks of construction, stability, price direction and agreement with sales and with LightGBM, yet its lifts are 1.33 to 1.40 times the truth when merchants plan into high-demand weeks, and 1.23 to 1.42 times in eight variants of that world. It still picks the right weeks to promote, but stock ordered to its lift is off by 0.44 to 0.48 of the true lift. papers.title: Newton-PINet: A fast physics-informed neural network with Newton linearization for meta-learning nonlinear PDEs
papers.abstract: Scientific machine learning has opened new avenues for solving parameterized partial differential equations (PDEs), enabling models to learn a family of PDEs and generalize to unseen instances. In this context, data-driven operator learning methods typically require large training datasets, while physics-informed neural networks (PINNs) suffer from difficult optimization and limited generalization, especially for nonlinear PDEs. We propose Newton-PINet, a physics-informed network enhanced by Newton linearization, offering an effective meta-learning framework for nonlinear PDEs. papers.title: SynthDCB: World Distillation for Scalable Device Control Benchmarking
papers.abstract: Scaling device-control evaluation requires scaling both the worlds agents interact with and the tasks they must solve. We introduce SynthDCB, a scalable benchmark for environment awareness and device control built through world distillation. World distillation transforms knowledge of device behaviors, interaction constraints, and environmental effects into modular executable components, which are composed into interactive worlds with explicit states, actions, and temporal dynamics. A unified capability representation connects tool discovery, world execution, and task synthesis, allowing new capabilities to enter evaluation through a shared construction pipeline. SynthDCB instantiates Home, Car, and Phone domains with 114 device classes, 1,166 functions, and 95 events, supporting five task families with 32 subtypes. The stateful design enables task validation and agent evaluation through

papers.title: Brain AI Scientist: An Evidence-Based Multi-Agent System for Translational Neuroimaging in Precision Psychiatry
papers.abstract: Resting-state functional magnetic resonance imaging (rs-fMRI) has revealed widespread brain-network alterations in psychiatric disorders, yet translating these findings into individualized clinical decision support remains challenging. Here we introduce Brain AI Scientist, an autonomous multi-agent framework that integrates patient-specific fMRI, clinical information, and scientific evidence through retrieval, verification, and prioritization. Guided by Research Domain Criteria and evidence-based medicine, it builds traceable chains linking phenotypes, anatomical abnormalities, biomarkers, mechanisms, interventions, and validation strategies. papers.title: When Helpful Agents Cause Financial Harm: Evaluating LLM Agent Safety in Executable Economic Worlds
papers.abstract: As LLM agents become increasingly capable of making consequential economic decisions, their safety under economic pressures remains poorly understood. We introduce EconSafeBench, the first benchmark for systematically evaluating the safety of LLM agents in executable economic environments. EconSafeBench contains 828 cases across five economic scenarios and four categories of safety violations. A key design is the matched evaluation of three sources of safety pressure, including explicit user requests, pressure from other actors, and pressure arising from the agent's own pursuit of a performance objective. We further evaluate safety at both static and dynamic scales through 30-period interactions with persistent memory and matched controls. Across eight LLMs, all evaluated models exhibit safety violations on the static benchmark, with overall violation rates ranging from 8.5% to 40.6%. We

papers.title: ChartSync: A Benchmark for Visuo-Logical Cascading Chart Editing
papers.abstract: Generative image editing models struggle with structured statistical charts when data modifications require geometric synchronization. We formalize this task as Visuo-Logical Cascading Editing (VLCE). However, existing methods remain confined to localized text substitutions and struggle with dependency-aware cascading updates. To systematically evaluate this capability, we introduce ChartSync, an expert-validated benchmark constructed via a programmatic rendering pipeline that guarantees deterministic visuo-logical coupling for the ground truth. ChartSync comprises 870 triplets across 9 chart categories and 4 task types, including 235 geometry-coupled VLCE instances that specifically test cascading text-to-geometry synchronization. papers.title: One Question, Four Voices: How Advice for Alzheimer's Caregiving Differs Between Caregivers, Clinicians, and Large Language Models
papers.abstract: Online caregiver forums are an important source of emotional and informational support for Alzheimer's disease and related dementias (ADRD). We compare responses to 85 real caregiver questions from ALZConnected across four responder groups: peer caregivers, physicians, ChatGPT, and a retrieval-augmented CareGPT grounded in peer discussions. Using 28 measures spanning linguistic form, emotional support, informational support, and topic scope, we examine how these voices differ when answering the same questions. Peers provided time-anchored narratives and community grounding; clinicians offered concise, advice-forward, clinically bounded guidance; and LLMs produced a formal, verbose, highly structured consultation style. CareGPT showed minimal measurable separation from ChatGPT, suggesting that retrieval plus prompt injection alone was insufficient to shift communicative stance. LLM output

papers.title: Understanding Failures in LLM Reasoning by Learning Structured Representations of Chain-of-Thought
papers.abstract: Chain-of-Thought (CoT) is central to improving reasoning in large language models, yet existing evaluation methods focus on step-level signals and ignore the underlying structure of reasoning traces. This raises a key question: what aspects of reasoning quality (i.e., correctness, efficiency, and failure patterns) are encoded in the structure of a CoT trace? We introduce \textbf{CoT2Graph}, a framework that represents CoT traces as directed dependency graphs, making relationships between reasoning steps explicit and capturing patterns such as backtracking, branching, and subtask merging. We model these graphs with graph neural networks and use attribution-based explanations to identify structural patterns associated with reasoning quality. papers.title: Evaluation-Free Recursive Self-Improvement for Coding Agents
papers.abstract: Recent self-improving coding agents have achieved strong benchmark performance by iteratively modifying their own executable implementations. A common pattern uses downstream task-derived evidence to decide which candidates or lineages continue evolving, which we term evaluate-and-select. Obtaining this signal requires repeatedly executing evolved agents on downstream tasks, so broader exploration incurs increasing evaluation cost, while repeated optimization against a fixed evaluation distribution may encourage benchmark-specific adaptation. We ask: can coding agents self-improve without downstream task evaluation inside the evolution loop? We introduce Explore-then-Integrate (ELITE), which integrates implementation mechanisms rather than selecting a single exploratory child to continue the lineage. At each generation, ELITE proposes diverse focused improvements, implements them indepen

papers.title: From Repositories to Training Environments: Scaling Long-Horizon Coding Agents with Environment Evolution Loop
papers.abstract: Training coding agents for long-horizon tasks requires environments with verifiable feedback. Existing pipelines often follow a linear process that ends with validation, establishing usability but providing little guidance on improving training value. Recursive self-improvement (RSI) often requires model rollouts or model training followed by downstream evaluation, with costs and feedback delays amplified on long-horizon tasks. How can we use timely, reliable proxy signals to improve training value and synthesize environments at scale? We present RepoFactory, an automated pipeline that converts real repositories into verifiable environments where agents build complete projects from scratch given a language specification. Its Environment Evolution Loop optimizes a multiplicative objective combining validity, structural coupling, and implementation scope through proxy feedback. RepoFactory

papers.title: EmoTrace: Recursive Trace-Factorized Generation for Emotional Support Conversation
papers.abstract: Fundamental to effective emotional support is the iterative interpersonal dynamic wherein a supporter intervention continuously shapes the psychological trajectory of the seeker. While contemporary models capture variables at the turn level, including transient emotions and discrete strategies, they inherently treat these factors as isolated events. By retaining strictly literal dialogue histories while discarding the underlying decision logic, such architectures remain fundamentally incapable of sustaining coherent extended support. Here we introduce EmoTrace, a recursive method utilizing trace factorization to preserve explicit decision continuity throughout interactions spanning multiple turns. Departing from others, our approach formulates each conversational turn as a structured interaction increment encapsulating the evolving state of the seeker, the selected strategy, the affect o

papers.title: Intrinsic Attention as Navigator: A Non-Generative Retrieval Method for Multi-Hop Queries
papers.abstract: For multi-hop queries in retrieval-augmented generation (RAG), it is crucial to accurately obtain evidence pieces. In this study, we propose a training-free method for multi-hop query retrieval, named Intrinsic Navigating-based Non-Generative Retrieval (IN-Retriever). Instead of generating intermediate reasoning text, the method extracts the bridging clue from the internal attention of the embedding model based on the current context and retrieved candidate documents. During iterative clue extraction and document retrieval, IN-Retriever strips away revealed clues from the embedded query vector and then reranks candidate documents in a targeted manner, thereby steering retrieval toward hidden next-hop evidence. papers.title: Syllable- and Word-Level Evaluation of Tibetan OCR
papers.abstract: Optical character recognition (OCR) for Tibetan is evaluated predominantly by character error rate (CER). Tibetan marks syllable boundaries but does not mark word boundaries, so a word error rate requires a segmenter. This study evaluates nine recognizer configurations on typeset, woodblock and two handwritten script styles, alone and in combination, and reports syllable- and word-level error rates, to our knowledge the first for Tibetan OCR. The configurations span CTC models, TrOCR encoder-decoders with and without post-training quantization, and a vision-language model, and each is scored under CER, the syllable error rate (SER) and three segmented word error rates (SWER). CER ranks systems largely as the higher-level rates do (Kendall $τ\geq 0.833$), with one pair ordered oppositely. papers.title: Validating LLM-Based Essay Scorers: A Comparative Analysis in Critical Online Reasoning in Medical Education
papers.abstract: Automated essay scorers (AES) based on large language models (LLMs) promise human-level accuracy. However, training, fine-tuning, and evaluating LLMs for specific assessment tasks is costly. In particular, the question arises whether these AES should be trained for specific domains or whether models based on generic LLMs might be sufficient. Human annotations, by contrast, are often more valid but far more expensive. This study evaluates whether ensembles of AES systems based on general-purpose LLMs can approximate human ratings of medical-education writing tasks by leveraging encoded linguistic and conceptual knowledge. The goal is to assess whether general-purpose models are applicable for assisting or potentially replacing human annotation in this domain. We experiment with 11 AES systems and 8 different LLMs and evaluate 668 student responses to 12 tasks, using \numprint{2076} evalua

papers.title: FlashREINFORCE: Critic-Free Single-Rollout Asynchronous RL for Agentic Language Models
papers.abstract: Asynchronous reinforcement learning suits long-horizon agents with irregular rollout times, but group-relative updates require repeated rollouts of each prompt. However, group-based sampling limits prompt coverage at a fixed rollout budget and introduces group synchronization barriers. One rollout per prompt avoids these constraints but removes the variance-reducing group baseline, making updates noisier and more prone to instability on stale, variable-length trajectories. We present FlashREINFORCE, a critic-free, one-pass framework built on One-Batch REINFORCE, a Sequence Trust Region, and Sample-Mean Optimization. These components preserve prompt coverage and signed feedback while controlling policy drift and length-amplified negative updates. papers.title: Retrieval-Augmented Generation for Clinical Decision Support in Gait Analysis: A Proof-of-Concept
papers.abstract: Large language models (LLMs) demonstrate significant potential for clinical decision support but lack specialized biomechanical knowledge required for accurate gait analysis interpretation. We developed and evaluated a Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) framework to enhance LLM-generated clinical explanations for ankle fracture rehabilitation using ground reaction force data. Using the GaitRec dataset (503 subjects: 211 healthy, 292 ankle fracture patients), we implemented a five-stage pipeline integrating: (1) machine learning classification (91.3\% accuracy); (2) Layer-wise Relevance Propagation for explainable feature identification; (3) RAG knowledge base from peer-reviewed biomechanics literature; (4) GPT-5 explanation generation with and without retrieval augmentation; and (5) double-blind evaluation by experienced physical therapists across five clinical criteria. papers.title: Where Language Models Fail Like Aphasic Patients and Where They Don't
papers.abstract: The computational architecture of human word production -- whether semantic-lexical retrieval and phonological encoding constitute dissociable processing stages -- has been debated for decades using hand-designed models with small vocabularies. We introduce computational architectural dissociation: using known architectural properties of vision-language models (VLMs) to derive falsifiable predictions about which patient error types should and should not align with model errors under perturbation. Because VLMs perform picture naming through learned semantic competition over full vocabularies but lack phonological encoding entirely, perturbation-induced errors should match patient patterns for semantic-stage categories but not phonological ones. papers.title: Keep it Simple! A Multiple-Choice Task can Benefit Generative Recommendation
papers.abstract: Sequential recommendation has recently witnessed growing interest in generative retrieval. One of the most popular approaches is to autoregressively generate the semantic identifiers (SIDs) of items as recommendations. Existing efforts mainly rely on semantic alignment, sophisticated architectural designs, and extensive hyperparameter tuning. However, the conventional learning framework for generative models could have foundational limitations. Specifically, most generative models directly predict target items without explicitly learning negative compositions and relative ranking signals. This is not well aligned with the philosophy of Bayesian personalized ranking (BPR), which emphasizes the importance of relative rankings between positive and negative samples. In this paper, we show that adding a simple multiple-choice auxiliary task into the learning objective can effectively address

papers.title: STA: A Split Temporal Adversary Method for Evaluating Robustness of Multimodal RL-based Driving Policies
papers.abstract: Multimodal reinforcement learning (MRL) offers a promising paradigm for autonomous driving by jointly leveraging complementary sensor observations to learn effective decision-making policies. However, its effectiveness critically depends on temporal alignment across modalities, making temporal inconsistency a fundamental vulnerability. Even subtle misalignment or latency can corrupt fused representations and ultimately lead to decision failures. Existing studies have explored adversarial attacks to induce cross-modal temporal inconsistencies, thereby enabling systematic evaluation of the temporal robustness of MRL policies. However, existing methods remain limited in generality, realism, and adaptivity. To address these limitations, we propose the Split Temporal Adversary (STA), which formulates multimodal temporal attacks as a unified decision process that jointly optimizes attack timin

papers.title: LLMs in DevSecOps: A Systematic Mapping of Models, Evidence, and Research Gaps Across the Software Lifecycle
papers.abstract: Large language models (LLMs) are increasingly being integrated into software security and DevSecOps workflows, yet their adoption, evaluation, and maturity vary substantially across lifecycle stages. This study systematically maps recent LLM-enabled security research published between 2024 and 2026 (until June) across six DevSecOps stages: \textit{Plan}, \textit{Code}, \textit{Test}, \textit{Review}, \textit{Deploy}, and \textit{Monitor}. For each stage, we analyze the security tasks addressed, models and adaptation strategies employed, evaluation settings, reported effectiveness, and key limitations. Our findings reveal an uneven research landscape, with \textit{Test} and \textit{Code} receiving substantially greater attention than \textit{Deploy} and \textit{Review}. Across stages, recent systems increasingly rely on structured context, iterative reasoning, fine-tuning, retrieval augme

papers.title: Loop Engineering: Version-Bound, Evidence-Gated Coordination for Production Coding Agents
papers.abstract: Coding agents can edit repositories and execute tests, yet production software work extends far beyond code generation. It requires durable task context, scoped authority, version-aware approval, source-independent verification, interruption recovery, and accountable handoffs between humans and automated workers. We present Loop Engineering, a method for operating multiple asynchronous agent loops over shared, auditable repository state without relying on private conversational handoffs. Each loop is specified by six elements: a trigger, a context projection, an authority boundary, a verifier, a stop condition, and a write-back rule. Versioned procedural contracts, called Skills, encode reusable operating policy; a Harness bounds the available action surface and collects evidence; human gates authorize high-consequence transitions against exact artifact versions. We report a design-and-e

papers.title: Wildfire-SSR: Geolocation-Aware Multimodal Fusion for Structure-Level Wildfire Risk Assessment
papers.abstract: Structure-level wildfire vulnerability assessment is critical for reducing losses in wildland-urban interface communities, yet existing methods often fail to combine parcel-scale ignition pathways with community-scale geographic coverage. This study introduces Wildfire-SSR (Satellite and Street-view for wildfire Risk), a geolocation-aware multimodal framework that integrates macro-scale satellite context with micro-scale street-view evidence. A Vision-Language Model extracts wildfire-relevant building and site attributes from pre-event street-view panoramas and converts them into structured semantic text. These features are spatially aligned with satellite imagery through a decoupled cross-attention fusion decoder, while a frozen satellite-pretrained DINOv3 encoder captures overhead visual context. Alternative geolocation embedding strategies are evaluated to anchor text-derived features

papers.title: VideoNexus: Video Perception Beyond the Reasoning Context
papers.abstract: Understanding long videos requires locating evidence, resolving visual details, and integrating observations into an answer. Even when relevant evidence is present, performing these operations within long, dense visual sequences burdens both perception and reasoning. Video agents enable selective inspection, but returning frames to the planner still accumulates visual information in its reasoning context. Delegating perception reduces this burden, yet sparse sampling can miss decisive details, and per-frame descriptions can preserve context growth. We introduce VideoNexus, a training-free framework that separates detailed video perception from evidence-driven planning and reasoning. The planner controls where to inspect, what to resolve, and how densely to sample. Perception sub-agents process native audio-video in independent contexts and return compact, temporally grounded evidence for

papers.title: ALIVE: Making Streaming Video Models Interactive
papers.abstract: Streaming video LLMs can continuously observe the world, yet often handle user requests in isolation. We introduce ALIVE, an interactive streaming video model supporting proactive monitoring, streaming task coordination, and feedback-seeking interaction. We construct ALIVE-SFT-288K and ALIVE-RL-3K for two-stage training. Contrastive supervised fine-tuning teaches when and how to respond, while reinforcement learning with Behavior-Aligned Credit Assignment (BACA) combines trajectory-level and local advantages to refine decisions, responses, and silence across multi-turn interactions. We also introduce FSI-Bench to evaluate feedback seeking and subsequent task completion. ALIVE achieves the highest overall scores among the compared models on four public benchmarks and FSI-Bench, demonstrating strong streaming understanding and interactive capabilities.

papers.title: FAVR: Flow-Aware Visual Residual Alignment for Vision-Language-Action Policies
papers.abstract: Pretrained video representations provide rich temporal information for robotic manipulation, yet effectively integrating them into existing vision-language-action (VLA) policies remains challenging. We present Flow-Aware Visual Residual Alignment (FAVR), a lightweight framework for flow-aware visual conditioning of frozen VLA policies. FAVR maintains a compact temporal visual state through linear Test-Time Training (TTT) and retrieves action-conditioned visual features throughout flow-based action generation. By exploiting the affine structure of the frozen action head, we explicitly characterize how injected visual features influence predicted action velocities and formulate flow-aware channel selection as a box-constrained optimization problem. We develop a FISTA-based solver for joint gate optimization and derive an efficient closed-form approximation through diagonalization and resca

papers.title: SciWorldBench: Do Video World Models Really Understand Scientific Experiments?
papers.abstract: While the ability of video generation models to accurately depict scientific phenomena has received growing attention, determining whether these models genuinely understand the underlying principles remains a critical challenge. Existing benchmarks typically evaluate video samples in isolation, making it difficult to expose models that simply fit superficial visual priors. In scientific experiments, a small change in one condition produces a markedly different outcome even when the rest of the setup remains fixed. Capitalizing on this sensitivity, we introduce SciWorldBench, a benchmark comprising paired scientific experiments. Each pair varies a single condition in an otherwise fixed setup, yielding two mutually exclusive expected outcomes. Each generation prompt specifies the condition but omits the expected outcome. We evaluate ten text-and-image-to-video (TI2V) models using an indepe

papers.title: BLIP-Live: Balancing Timeliness & Firing Precision in Proactive Streaming Video Agents
papers.abstract: Streaming video understanding is becoming increasingly important for real-world interactive systems. Such systems must be proactive for natural and useful human interaction: they should respond as soon as sufficient evidence becomes available while avoiding premature, redundant, or incorrect responses. We present BLIP-Live, a framework unifying data, metrics, harness, and training around a shared formulation of proactivity as effective causal response decisions balancing the two competing objectives of responding vs silence. First, we construct BLIP-Live-780K dataset containing human annotations of proactive response content and timing, which defines this desired behavior. We then propose PAUC-F, a metric to effectively measure our desired proactive behavior. PAUC-F combines existing response timeliness metrics with firing precision to reward early useful responses without rewarding exce

papers.title: MedJev: A System One Vision-Language Decision Model for Fast and Effective Medical Image Understanding
papers.abstract: Medical image understanding with vision-language models (VLMs) typically relies on autoregressively generating reasoning and answer tokens. These unnecessary tokens make the inference cost scale with the response length and force the answer to be parsed from free-form text, incurring avoidable latency and decision errors. To this end, we introduce \textsc{MedJev}, a \emph{system one} vision-language decision model that maps medical images, questions, and candidate answers directly to decisions in a single multimodal forward pass, without any autoregressive generation process. For fast inference, \textsc{MedJev} removes the upper language layers and the generative output pathway, while keeping the full vision pathway and all visual tokens. On this shortened backbone, a decision head scores each candidate by pretrained query--key matching and refines the scores with a lightweight multilaye

papers.title: MedicalDPO: Multi-Objective Direct Preference Optimization for CT to PET Translation
papers.abstract: CT-to-PET synthesis estimates functional PET images from anatomical CT scans for auxiliary analysis, representation pretraining, and missing-modality completion. Brownian Bridge diffusion models can produce multiple PET candidates of different quality under the same CT condition, exposing an intra-condition quality hierarchy. Candidate quality spans complementary spatial, structural, and intensity dimensions, while DPO-only fine-tuning may compromise absolute synthesis fidelity. We propose MedicalDPO which converts this hierarchy into preference supervision automatically constructed from paired CT-PET training data. Multiple candidates are ranked across the three fidelity dimensions, and strict cross-metric verification retains preferred-rejected pairs with consistent quality separation. Relative denoising-error preference optimization is jointly trained with the original Brownian Bridge

papers.title: Visual Marking as a Native Reasoning Capability for Multimodal LLMs
papers.abstract: Visual reasoning often requires maintaining intermediate spatial states that are difficult to express in text. Existing approaches either rely on external drawing tools or image generators, or encode these states in latent tokens without explicit spatial correspondence to the input image. We introduce SelfMark, which enables MLLMs to construct and use visual marks directly in their native visual feature space. By treating the visual token grid as a canvas, SelfMark establishes explicit spatial correspondence between marks and images. This is achieved through a locate-mark-read procedure, where the model identifies relevant locations, constructs task-dependent mark features, and reads the resulting visual features to guide its reasoning. papers.title: VisDrone-ReID: A Unified Multi-Category Object Re-Identification Benchmark
papers.abstract: Object re-identification (Re-ID) benchmarks remain predominantly confined to single-category evaluations, limiting the development of unified systems capable of operating across diverse object types. This paper presents VisDrone-ReID, a unified multi-category Re-ID benchmark derived from the VisDrone2019-MOT dataset through a principled conversion pipeline. The pipeline resolves structural incompatibilities between multi-object tracking annotations and Re-ID evaluation requirements, addressing sequence-scoped identity collision, temporal redundancy, and the absence of a principled identity-level train/test split. The resulting benchmark comprises 9,516 identities and 150,016 images across ten object categories - pedestrian, people, bicycle, car, van, truck, tricycle, awning-tricycle, bus, and motor, sourced from 80 unmanned aerial vehicle (UAV) sequences captured across urban environment

papers.title: Learning a Task-Adaptive Low-Dimensional Semantic Space for Improved Visual Classification
papers.abstract: Semantic visual classification commonly aligns visual embeddings with semantic spaces induced by pretrained text encoders. However, such spaces are typically high-dimensional, weakly aligned with visual feature geometry, and insufficiently discriminative for downstream classification tasks. We propose TaSS, a framework for learning a task-adaptive low-dimensional semantic space that preserves semantic structure while explicitly optimizing class separability. TaSS is constructed through a parameterized geometry transformation of pretrained text embeddings that enlarges inter-class margins via distance reshaping and improves intra-class compactness through prototype-preserving semantic constraints. The resulting semantic space maintains meaningful semantic relationships while producing a discriminative geometry tailored for classification. Frozen visual encoder features are subsequently al

papers.title: UnSPAD: Uncertainty-aware Single Photon Burst Photography
papers.abstract: We introduce UnSPAD, an uncertainty-aware burst photography framework capable of fusing and denoising arbitrarily long sequences of binary single photon avalanche diode (SPAD) measurements. Unlike prior methods that require fixed burst lengths or rely on powerful generative priors, UnSPAD combines learned motion estimation with uncertainty-informed measurement fusion and denoising to produce temporally consistent, hallucination-free reconstructions. UnSPAD first forms an initial scene estimate by averaging flow-aligned binary frames. UnSPAD then uses per-pixel uncertainty maps to perform uncertainty-aware denoising; the denoiser is informed about which regions accumulated the fewest observations (and thus contain the most relative shot noise) due to motion, occlusion, or alignment errors. papers.title: RoboACE: Adversarial Co-Evolution for Robot Self-Improvement
papers.abstract: Robot agents can improve reusable skills, planning procedures, and recovery strategies from execution feedback, yet a fixed practice source leaves the search for new weaknesses unchanged. Useful practice depends on the agent's current capabilities, so the procedure that chooses practice must also be revisable. We present RoboACE (Robot Adversarial Co-Evolution), a framework that jointly evolves curriculum and execution harnesses around frozen foundation models. The curriculum harness uses accumulated capability evidence to propose informative challenges, while the execution harness responds with reusable revisions that expand execution capabilities. Alternating updates hold one side fixed as the other changes, and admitted challenges form fixed snapshots for comparing execution revisions. Starting from a compact set of LIBERO practice conditions, the resulting frozen deployment outperfor

papers.title: HEAMS: Holistic Evaluation of Agent Memory Systems
papers.abstract: Memory systems allow AI agents to persist information across interactions, making them more personalized and more capable on long-horizon tasks. This persistence introduces new risks: stored information can be disclosed in inappropriate contexts, resist correction or deletion, be retained beyond what users desire, or be poisoned to influence later agent behaviour. Yet memory systems are typically evaluated on task performance and efficiency alone. We argue that a memory system should instead be understood as the custodian of its user's persistent information, with responsibilities that extend beyond helping an agent complete its tasks, and that it should be evaluated holistically against all such responsibilities. We present Holistic Evaluation of Agent Memory Systems (HEAMS), an open-source framework for evaluating agent memory systems in this way. First, we state the responsibilities o

papers.title: Autonomous Multi-modal Agents for ITOps Observability
papers.abstract: ITOps observability products must integrate data from different tools and systems. We present ITOps Observability Studio, a multi-modal multi-agent system that orchestrates observability workflows through collaborative AI agents. Its three-tier architecture features inter-agent communication, specialized LLM-powered agents for data access, schema operations and visualization, and unified tool integration. The system supports natural language to GraphQL translation, GraphQL schema generation, schema mapping, trace data lifecycle management and multi-tool workflows for reliability engineering. Its agents are instrumented with agent analytics, so that their model and tool calls can be traced. We evaluate each agent on its own benchmark, scored against gold answers where they exist and by a model judge for schema mapping and chart quality. papers.title: DetouR: Plugging Association Routes into Search Agents for Multi-hop Question Answering
papers.abstract: Search agents answer multi-hop questions by interleaving reasoning with retrieval, deciding at each step what to search next. Existing agents follow semantic routes: they infer what is missing and phrase it as a query, reaching only what the model can name. Yet the decisive page is often one the question never names, frequently just one hyperlink away from evidence already retrieved. Following such association routes reaches more gold pages than semantic search under the same budget. Exploiting them raises two challenges: obtaining the association structure without costly offline graph construction, and keeping linked evidence in the reader's limited context, where relevance- and fusion-based selection discards it. We propose DetouR, a plug-in that reuses the links arriving with retrieved pages and adds no search or LLM call. Link Rerouting replaces near-repeat queries with routes to lin

papers.title: Reflection Is Not Always Worth It: Budgeted Reflection Allocation for Recommendation Agents
papers.abstract: This work aims to make recommendation agents more efficient by reducing unnecessary LLM reflection while preserving full-catalog ranking and inference reranking. Since BRAVE changes only how training-time reflection is allocated, it does not introduce new user data requirements or additional LLM exposure beyond the base agent protocol. The main potential risk is that a poorly calibrated allocator may assign less reflection to users whose preferences are sparse, niche, or under-represented, which could weaken personalization for those users or indirectly affect item exposure. This risk can be mitigated through deployment-time auditing and conservative allocation design. In practice, reflection budgets should be evaluated not only by aggregate Recall or NDCG, but also across user-history lengths, item popularity groups, and application-relevant cohorts when such analysis is permitted. papers.title: Fine-Grained RLAIF for Visual Safety: Learning to Zoom into Hazards for Multimodal Safety Alignment
papers.abstract: Recent multimodal safety alignment heavily relies on a text-centric paradigm, assuming risks are explicit in language or globally prominent in images. However, real-world hazards are often visually subtle or peripheral, causing existing models to fail due to their reliance on coarse, global visual representations. In this work, we study fine-grained visual safety alignment and introduce a challenging 1,200-sample benchmark across four domains, where hazards necessitate localized inspection. To address this, we propose Fine-Grained RLAIF (FGR), a reinforcement learning framework that casts image zoom-in as a learnable perception policy. FGR employs a decomposed reward design to jointly align three core safety behaviors: (i) where to look via a visual evidence reward, (ii) when to act via a tool-formatting constraint, and (iii) how to reason via visually grounded safety explanations. papers.title: When AI Agents Should Repair, Replan, or Abandon: A Threshold Theory of Plan Commitment
papers.abstract: AI agents often discover mid-execution that their plan is broken, for example when an action fails or a tool is withdrawn. Deployed systems use conventions such as retry loops or "always replan," and a recent benchmark finds no fixed strategy dominates. This paper derives the optimal policy. In the model, a disruption destroys the causal support of part of a plan; repair is a partial reset that preserves the plan's structure, replanning is a full reset, and changing a plan is costly because others have conditioned on it. The optimal policy is a threshold in effective disruption depth: repair shallow damage, replan after deep damage, and abandon the goal when even a fresh plan is not worth its cost. papers.title: Well-Log Reconstruction with Pre-trained Geological Knowledge: A Knowledge-Conditioned Large-Language-Model Generative Agent
papers.abstract: Missing well-log intervals make subsurface reconstruction ill-posed. Existing numerical regression models lack geological prior knowledge to constrain ambiguous inverse mappings. We propose GeoLog-Agent, a knowledge-conditioned generative agent using pre-trained large language models (LLMs) as a source of geological priors. A universal Geo-Harness translates LLM stratigraphic reasoning into formation-anchored petrophysical trajectories, feature-wise linear modulation, and conditional adversarial constraints. On the Norwegian North Sea benchmark, GeoLog-Agent achieves a mean $R^2$ of 0.9307 and a peak $R^2$ of 0.9713. It exceeds the nine-baseline average $R^2$ of 0.8387 by 0.0920, with a 30.97% average RMSE reduction, and exceeds the strongest baseline by 0.0274--0.0498 in $R^2$, with 16.25%--24.05% lower RMSE. papers.title: Toward Planning Representations That Separate Task Structure from Visual Content
papers.abstract: Effective planning requires representations that preserve task-relevant geometry and object identity while ignoring visual variation that does not alter the task. Existing evaluations of visual generalization often change several factors simultaneously, making the source of a failure difficult to identify. We introduce a controlled evaluation of object-goal navigation (ObjectNav), the task of reaching an instance of a named object category, in procedurally generated ProcTHOR houses. Training and evaluation houses share floor plans, object locations, goals, and start states, while visual factors are changed individually or in combination. Across model-free reinforcement learning (RL), model-based RL, and agents using frozen pretrained visual representations, our results show that appearance changes impair navigation, but their effects differ sharply by factor. Surface material changes acc

papers.title: Agent Authenticator: Passkey-Grade, Hardware-Bound Authentication for AI Agents
papers.abstract: AI coding agents now push code, publish packages, call model APIs and operate cloud resources on behalf of developers. They authenticate to these services with the same bearer secrets humans use, personal access tokens, API keys and package-registry tokens, stored where the model, its subprocesses and any co-resident malware can read them. Incidents in 2025 and 2026, including prompt-injection attacks on coding agents and self-propagating supply-chain worms, show that this arrangement fails in predictable ways. Passkeys solved the analogous problem for humans, but they require a human gesture on every use and cannot be operated by an autonomous process. papers.title: Successive Convexification in Learned World Models for Safe Offline Planning
papers.abstract: World models learned from offline data allow an agent to plan without further interaction with the environment, but the sampling-based planners used with them handle safety constraints only by scoring or rejecting sampled action sequences. We instead pose safe planning in the latent space of a learned world model as a successive convex program (SCP), in which a learned discrete-time control barrier function is imposed as a constraint at every step of the horizon. SCP requires smooth dynamics, so we build the networks from smoothed MaxMin activations and spectrally normalised layers, and bound the resulting linearisation error in terms of the Lipschitz bound and the smoothing width. As SCP is a local method, we start it from a sampled plan. papers.title: Hardening Agentic Web Populations Through Multi-Criterion Competitive Co-Evolution: Lessons from Wargame Strategy Optimization
papers.abstract: Agents on the open web will face adversaries that keep adapting, so a defense that is only tested once will eventually be found and broken. We propose treating jailbreak attacks and safety guardrails as two populations that evolve against each other, rather than as a fixed attacker probing a fixed defense. This idea comes directly from wargame strategy optimization, where two-population competitive co-evolution with alternating evolution cycles and cross-play evaluation has already been shown to produce strategies that are robust to a moving opponent, and where a companion line of work has shown that the same machinery can measure how much competitive pressure a population must absorb. However, real-world applications can never rely on a single criterion as a key performance indicator, rather must use multiple conflicting criteria, such as, cost and efficiency. papers.title: Can an Agent Rethink What It Knows? Selective Scene Memory Updates in a Changing World
papers.abstract: Task configurations in factories, warehouses, and everyday physical environments change over time. Physical AI systems therefore need to incorporate new facts into scene memory while preserving valid information about equipment, objects, and operating constraints. We study updates to this parametric semantic-memory layer and present a joint evaluation of correction and preservation under finite update budgets. At fixed current fact count and memory parameter count, the protocol combines independent single-fact updates, budget trajectories, old-to-new answer diagnostics, and first stable success. Using a frozen 4B language model with late-layer LoRA, we evaluate seven preparation conditions and six update budgets on four-field synthetic semantic configurations. In two exposure-matched history conditions, increasing the budget from eight to 32 updates raises joint success from 6.25% to 94.

papers.title: What Moves a LoCoMo Score? Memory Context, Answer Prompts and Judges
papers.abstract: LoCoMo is a widely reported benchmark for long-term conversational memory, but published scores mix memory quality with choices of answer prompt, judge and baseline layout that are rarely reported together. We measure how much these choices move a score, and evaluate Becos, a team memory system for coding agents, as a black box under all of them: ten conversations (1,540 questions), two answer models (gpt-4o-mini, gpt-4.1-mini), two answer prompts and three LLM judges, against a whole-conversation baseline rerun under identical conditions. Changing only the judge moves a score by up to 7.2 points and changing only the answer prompt by up to 9.3. A blind human check of 150 answers finds the judges reliable when they agree, and the primary judge's errors on disputed answers working against Becos rather than for it. Becos answers from a context with 90% fewer characters than the whole conve

papers.title: FundingClaw: Automated Grant Proposal Writing Agents System
papers.abstract: Grant proposal writing remains a manual, labor-intensive bottleneck: proposals must satisfy rigid, agency-specific templates, and the same intellectual content must be repeatedly re-encoded into incompatible formats across funding organizations. We introduce FundingClaw, a multi-agent framework built on template-driven skill selection, where a Template Parser ingests any agency's specification and selects the appropriate writing skills for each stage, so that one research brief can produce compliant proposals for NSFC, NSF, KAKENHI, or ERC without modifying generation logic. A blueprint-skeleton strategy drafts a structured outline before any prose is written, mitigating the semantic drift that plagues long-form generation. Three sequential stages produce the rationale, research content, and research foundation sections, with multi-source verification of the PI's record and optional PDF-

papers.title: When the Mythical Man-Month Meets Agentic Web Systems: Structured Coordination for Scalable Development
papers.abstract: As agentic systems are increasingly deployed to support complex Web tasks, multi-agent architectures offer greater parallelism, specialization, and task coverage. However, increasing the number of agents does not necessarily improve system performance, as communication, synchronization, redundant work, and coordination overhead may offset the benefits of additional agents. This presents a fundamental scaling challenge for agentic Web systems: how can agent populations be organized to balance task performance and coordination costs? To address this challenge, we systematically investigate the relationship between agent population size, per-agent token consumption, and coordination overhead in collaborative agentic systems. Experiments on complex Web-oriented software development tasks reveal a non-linear scaling pattern: per-agent token consumption initially decreases as the agent populat

papers.title: Agent-Guided Process Verification for Mathematical Self-Correction
papers.abstract: Large language models have made substantial progress in mathematical reasoning, yet in complex multi-step reasoning, an error at any step may propagate along an incorrect path, and the resulting solution may omit necessary branches. Existing natural-language reflection methods often struggle to locate critical errors precisely, while outcome verification typically checks only whether the available candidate answers satisfy the problem conditions and can therefore overlook necessary branches. To address these limitations, we propose Agent-Guided Process Verification (AGPV) for mathematical self-correction. AGPV decomposes the current solution into an ordered sequence of key claims, verifies them individually while invoking a shared mathematical toolbox when needed, and stops upon detecting the first error. A summarization agent converts the failure evidence into a diagnosis that guides a

papers.title: Beyond Benchmarks: Evaluating Large Language Models and Agentic Patterns for Static Code Analysis Warning Classification
papers.abstract: Context: Static Code Analysis (SCA) tools support software verification and validation, reducing the time and cost of code reviews. However, the best SCA tools in the practitioner community generate a high volume of false positives, which developers tend to ignore, leading to genuine warnings being overlooked. Accordingly, studies increasingly adopt Large Language Models (LLMs) to identify and reduce false positives. Existing studies have produced promising results on public datasets, but underperformed on unseen datasets. Moreover, researchers do not leverage the full potential of Agentic patterns in LLMs or incorporate established code quality standards for warning classification. papers.title: Assume/Guarantee Contracts for the Compositional Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning of Heterogeneous Teams
papers.abstract: Multi-agent reinforcement learning (MARL) problems for heterogeneous teams require agents to collaborate to complete team tasks while making the best use of diverse agent capabilities. We introduce assume/guarantee contracts for heterogeneous multi-agent systems (AGC-MAS) and Iterative Heterogeneous Assignment for MARL (IHA-MARL). AGC-MAS contracts are compositional objects that encode the assumptions provided to, and the guarantees required of, each subtask contributing to the overall team task. We formulate contracts as tuples that specify a subtask, an automaton, timeout and success-probability requirements, and dispatch behavior. The automaton tracks an agent's high-level progress through the subtask associated with its contract and provides a natural mechanism for synchronization across contracts. papers.title: Ask Precisely, Assume Wisely: Interactive Evaluation of Ambiguity Resolution in Large Language Models
papers.abstract: Ambiguity is a core challenge in human--AI interaction, where models must decide when to make assumptions and when to seek clarification. Existing approaches to ambiguity evaluation largely focus on coverage over multiple interpretations using static metrics, offering limited insight into how efficiently a model converges toward a single user-intended interpretation through interaction. We introduce a preference-grounded simulated user framework for controlled, multi-turn evaluation of ambiguity resolution, grounding simulator responses strictly in user disambiguation preferences to avoid hallucination and over-disclosure. Alongside this, we define three observable dissatisfaction signals --- incorrect assumptions, repeating clarifications, and irrelevant clarifications --- that characterize interaction quality beyond task accuracy. Our analysis reveals a clear trade-off: models that fre

papers.title: We Have All the Cards: Securing Agent Cards at the Operational Trust Boundary of the Agent2Agent Protocol
papers.abstract: AI agent interoperability protocols enable orchestrators to discover and invoke external agents using machine-readable metadata. In the Agent2Agent (A2A) protocol, Agent Cards contain attacker-controllable natural-language fields that may influence agent selection before a provider is invoked, creating a pre-invocation trust problem. We characterize this discovery-time attack surface through a taxonomy of ten Agent Card manipulation attacks and present SECCARD, a layered validation framework combining protocol checks, deterministic analysis, and LLM-based semantic reasoning. We measure the emerging public A2A ecosystem by probing 36.1 million Internet domains and collecting 310 deployed Agent Cards. Two annotators independently label the corpus with 96.8% agreement. papers.title: SPLICE: Structured Prompt Local Iterative Combinatorial Evolution
papers.abstract: Natural language optimization (NLO) improves an agent by having a model critique and rewrite its natural language policy parameters: system prompts, tool instructions, reasoning directives, few-shot demonstrations. These artifacts are multi-section documents in which some sections encode contracts (safety clauses, tool schemas, output formats) that must not drift, while others are legitimate optimization targets. Most iterative NLO methods treat the artifact as a single editable string, producing three recurrent failure modes: unsafe global rewrites, beam collapse onto a single lineage, and unchecked bloat, none addressed by formal guarantees. We introduce SPLICE, a unified NLO framework that poses optimization as constrained combinatorial search over an edit graph of block-structured, selectively-mutable states. papers.title: Exstill: The Most Efficient Single-Chip Processor for the Next Token
papers.abstract: Generating a token with a language model requires a fixed amount of arithmetic, whose energy sets a floor beneath any hardware. For Qwen3-1.7B at a 16K-token context, gate-level measurements at 5 nm place this floor at 0.89 mJ per token, yet an NVIDIA B300 spends 391-1,120x that. The excess is the price of generality, software layers, programmable hardware and moving weights and key-value (KV) caches from external memory, and it widens with each process generation. We present a co-design approach that brings token generation close to this floor and then lowers the floor itself, optimizing silicon and model together in a gate-level search loop. Fixing one model architecture in the datapath, with weights still loadable, and holding weights and every conversation's KV cache on-die, a pre-silicon 5 nm design brings an unchanged Qwen3-1.7B token to 3.4x its floor. papers.title: Risk-certified prompt optimization for LLM-as-a-judge guardrails
papers.abstract: LLM-as-a-judge guardrails are often controlled primarily through system prompts, yet standard prompt optimization methods target average performance rather than explicit safety constraints. This paper studies system-prompt selection as a constrained optimization problem: maximize benign pass rate while keeping the missed-attack rate below a user-specified level α with finite-sample statistical control. The framework combines LLM-based judging, automatic prompt generation, and distribution-free risk certification. This work instantiates it in two procedures: CPS and CRISP. CPS generates a fixed pool of prompts from training data, then certifies candidates on a held-out evaluation set using simultaneous upper confidence bounds and selects the certified prompt with the highest benign utility. CRISP instead integrates risk feedback into an adaptive search, using hard example-guided rewriting

papers.title: Low-Latency LLM-Based Streaming Multi-Talker ASR with Verifiable Rewards
papers.abstract: LLM-based architectures offer strong generalization and instruction-following capabilities for streaming automatic speech recognition (ASR), but multi-talker use introduces coupled transcription, attribution, and latency challenges. Our wearable setting requires real-time transcription of a conversation between a near-field device wearer and a far-field partner. Because partial hypotheses are rendered on persistent sides of a dialogue UI, speaker roles cannot be permuted and each speaker tag must precede its turn. These sparse tags are weakly optimized by supervised fine-tuning (SFT), while committing to a leading tag can delay the text that follows. We therefore post-train a streaming LLM-based ASR model with reinforcement learning with verifiable rewards (RLVR), combining a fixed-role Speaker-Attributed WER (SA-WER) grader with a turn-level onset-delay reward. papers.title: LongCat-Video-Avatar 1.6 Technical Report
papers.abstract: Recent advances in audio-driven avatar video generation have enabled increasingly realistic synthesis, yet achieving precise lip-audio synchronization, natural, human-like motion, and visual consistency over long sequences remains challenging. We present LongCat-Video-Avatar 1.6, which builds on LongCat-Video-Avatar 1.5 to improve expressive naturalness and reduce error accumulation during extended generation, e.g., exaggerated lip movements and overly red, temporally unstable lip coloration, enhance the naturalness of facial expressions and coordinated head and body movements. These improvements are driven by a refined post-training pipeline that integrates reinforcement learning, improved classifier-free guidance strategies for DMD-based few-step distillation, long-video rollouts, and on-policy distillation.
